qc_05_cantons_de_l_est.blurb: The Cantons-de-l'Est region of Quebec, centered on the Sherbrooke area, mixes sport and trad with a good amount of top-roping. Mount Orford is the largest crag, a steep sport cliff on gneiss that is solid but can feel sharp on crimps, with some sections staying wet. Most of its routes sit between 5.9 and 5.13, with a few easier lines. Lac Larouche is a smaller, mainly traditional crag with natural protection that is sometimes hard to place, and its routes cluster from 5.8 to 5.10 with easy top-rope setups. Mont Pinacle adds more trad. Overall the grades run from 5.5 to the low 5.14s, centered near 5.10, with a little bouldering and a few ice and mixed lines.

wa_treasury.blurb: A forested bouldering venue in the Skykomish Valley, in the central-west Cascades at about 3,200 feet. Everything here is bouldering, close to two hundred problems, from V0 up to V10, with most between V0 and V4 and a steady taper above. The 2nd Field (Main) holds the great majority, including the Whiteface and Semantics areas, and the 1st Field has the rest. The setting is lush, with ferns, a stream crossing and a short hike through talus and trees. Most blocks catch midday sun, though the River Boulder stays shady all day. Snow keeps it out of reach through winter and spring, with the season typically opening in late June or early July, and mosquitoes and biting flies can be fierce.

id_swan_falls.blurb: Basalt boulder fields on the east side of the Snake River canyon, southwest of Boise in West Idaho. The roughly two hundred problems are all bouldering, running from VB to V9, with most between V0 and V3 and a solid group at V6 and V7. Walks from the car take about 5 to 15 minutes. There are no trees for shade, and the eastern cliffs block the morning sun, so spring, autumn and winter are the main seasons, with early summer mornings also workable. The biggest clusters are the Black Slabbath Area, Spice Girls Area, Hairpin Boulders and the Taj Mahal, and there are over twenty smaller groups spread through the canyon.

nm_southern_box_areas.blurb: The southern part of the Box, a rhyolite canyon complex near Socorro in the high desert at about 5,800 feet, roughly an hour south of Albuquerque. The stone is of mixed quality, though much of it is solid. Sport climbing makes up about three fifths of the routes here, with a good amount of bouldering and a small trad share. Sport lines run mostly from 5.9 to 5.12, with the most at 5.10, plus easier options and a few 5.13s, while boulders range from V0 to V10. Major Wall, Scarry Wall, Minor Wall and Alcohol Wall are the main crags. Winter days are comfortable, summer is hot and buggy, and several sport faces stay shady in the morning or afternoon.

nc_looking_glass_rock.blurb: A 600-foot granite monolith in Pisgah National Forest near Brevard, and one of the most iconic climbing destinations in the Southeast. The climbing is overwhelmingly traditional and often multi-pitch, with a few aid lines on the North Side and a boulder area at the base. Grades run from about 5.5 to 5.13, with most between 5.9 and 5.12 and the largest group at 5.10. The Nose Area and Sun Wall are known for free climbing up roof-like features, while the Hidden Wall favors technical edging and face moves. Fall and winter are the best seasons, and the North Side and Hidden Wall stay shady enough for summer. Many routes need two ropes to descend.
